comparisons.reason: Left counts only direct quotations (verbatim or near-verbatim excerpts) of OP text. Right also counts explicit references to a specific OP sentence, claim, example or passage, such as 'you said X' or 'your point about Y', without a quote. That makes right a broader construct. Left explicitly says paraphrases don't count, while right accepts close paraphrase and referencing. The empty-list rules also differ: left gives 0 for a valid empty list, while right gives 0 only for a nonempty list and appears to treat an empty list as null.
